name: float-near-critical
title: Float and near-critical
description: Total float profile of a P6 project: float statistics, distribution by range, the float paths of the last F9 and the near-critical activities (total float above 0 and within a few days). Use when the user asks about float, near-critical work, float paths or how much float the schedule has left.

args.name: project
args.description: Project ID as shown in P6

args.name: near_days
args.description: Near-critical threshold: total float above 0 and at or below this many days (each activity's calendar); 10 when the user gives none

template:
Float and near-critical activities of project {project}: total float statistics and distribution, the float paths of the last F9 and the near-critical activities (total float above 0 and at or below {near_days} days; near_days is 10 when the user gives none). Nothing is written to the database.

This skill gives you every figure: you copy fields, you never compute them.
- reference/spec.json: the calls, the slots (each a field of one call) and the tables.
- reference/fields.md: for every slot and table column, its field, unit, format and meaning.
- reference/report.md: the report to fill.
- reference/checks.md: stop rules and checks to run before answering.
- reference/example.md: the report filled on a demo project (an example of the format, not of the figures).

Calls, in this order. Each call is one page: the report shows that page and says when there are more,
so do not read further pages.
1. fa = p6_float_analysis(project="{project}"): float statistics and distribution of the open activities, data date.
2. fp = p6_float_paths(project="{project}", limit=30): float paths of the last F9: summary per path and the activities in path order.
3. nc = p6_critical_path(project="{project}", float_threshold_days={near_days}, min_float_days=0, limit=30): near-critical activities: total float above 0 and at or below near_days; project counts.

Write the report:
1. Start from reference/report.md. Replace each slot placeholder (a slot name in curly braces) by the field
   named in spec.json slots (call and path), written in the slot's format (reference/fields.md). An argument
   written <name> in these instructions is the placeholder of that name in curly braces in report.md and
   checks.md: the value given (an empty optional argument is left out of the calls).
2. Replace each line [table: name] by that table: one row per item of its list, in the order returned, at
   most its cap, every cell in its column's format, the heads as in spec.json. A table with a totals entry
   ends with its Total row, taken from the totals of its call, never from adding the rows. Only a table
   built from the rows list of its call ends, when that call has more pages (next_offset not null), with
   the line "Showing the first <returned> of <total> <noun>." (returned and total of that call). A table
   built from another list or dict of the call (weeks, paths, roots, causes, counts...) ends with "Only the
   first <cap> <noun> are shown." when that list is longer than the cap, and never with a Showing line. An
   empty list gives the table's empty text; a call that failed or was skipped gives no table.
3. Keep the lines between [if: slot] and [end if] only when the slot is true (true, a number other than 0,
   a text or list that is not empty, an ID - name whose ID is not null), the lines between [if not: slot]
   and [end if] only when it is not; remove the markers.
4. Numbers: take the number as written in the result and round it, halves away from zero, to the decimals
   of its format (-104274.95 in n1 is -104,275.0); whole numbers and counts take a comma between thousands
   (1,227), also in the Showing lines. A null value is written as the slot's or column's none text, and so
   is an ID - name whose ID is null.
5. Never add, subtract, divide, count rows or match rows of two results: a figure that is not a slot or a
   table cell is left out. Ignore the note fields of the tools unless a slot names them.
6. Write the headings and sentences in the user's language; keep values, IDs, names and number formats
   exactly as formatted.
7. Run reference/checks.md before answering. Report a failed cross-check, never hide it; say nothing about
   the checks that pass.

For this skill:
- Do not show the bucket samples. The warnings are the fixed sentences of report.md only.

# Float and near-critical activities of {project}

Data date {data_date}, last schedule run (F9) {last_f9}. Float of that run, in days of each activity's calendar.

[if: stale]
Warning: this project was changed after its last F9. Float, float paths and critical counts are out of date until it is rescheduled in P6 (F9).
[end if]

## Total float

- Open activities analysed: {activities} (not completed; LOE and WBS summary left out); without a total float: {no_tf}.
- Total float (d): minimum {tf_min}, maximum {tf_max}, mean {tf_mean}, median {tf_median}.
- Negative total float: {negative}; zero total float: {zero}; critical: {critical} ({critical_definition}).
- On the longest path (driving path flag): {longest_path}.
- Total float at or below {near_days} d, critical included: {within_near}.
- Near-critical, total float above 0 d and at or below {near_days} d: {near_total} ({near_definition}).
- Total floats that are not whole days: {tf_not_whole}.

[if: negative]
Warning: {negative} open activities have negative total float: they finish later than a constraint or the project must finish date allows.
[end if]
[if not: ranges_covered]
Warning: the range counts do not add up to the activities analysed: do not use the distribution below.
[end if]

## Float distribution

Ranges in days: [a, b) includes a and excludes b, (a, b] excludes a and includes b. Percentages of the {activities} open activities analysed.

[table: buckets]

## Float paths

Source: {fp_source} (float_path: P6's multiple float paths of the last F9; driving_path_flag: no float path stored).

[table: paths]

[table: path_rows]

## Near-critical activities (total float above 0 d and at or below {near_days} d)

By total float, then start. Activities with total float at or below 0 are left out of this table.

[table: near]

# Checks before answering

## Stop rules (write the sentence, then stop)

- A call says the project is not found: "Project <project> was not found: check the Project ID (p6_list_projects)."
- p6_float_analysis finds no open activity (scope.activities 0): "Project <project> has no open activity: there is no float to analyse." and stop.

## Cross-checks (each group must be equal)

1. fa.schedule_state.data_date = fp.schedule_state.data_date = nc.schedule_state.data_date (same data date).
2. fa.scope.activities = nc.counts.open (same open activities).
3. fa.stats.negative_tf = nc.counts.negative_float (same negative float count).

If one differs, the database changed between the calls: run the three calls again once. If it still
differs, say which pair differs and do not publish the figures it concerns.

## Before sending

- Every number, date and count is a slot or a table cell of reference/fields.md, copied from its field
  and written in its format. Nothing was added, subtracted, divided, counted or matched by you.
- The tables keep the rows in the order returned and stop at their cap (ranges 12, float paths 10,
  float path activities 30, near-critical 30). Every near-critical row has a total float above 0. A table whose call has more pages (next_offset not null)
  ends with its line "Showing the first <returned> of <total> ...", both numbers copied from that call.
- Every activity is written "Activity ID - name". A null float path or order is written "none".
- The bucket samples (tf_sample, ff_sample) are not shown: they carry Activity IDs without names.
- The warning blocks are kept only when their slot says so (stale true, negative not 0,
  ranges_covered false).
- Headings and sentences are in the user's language; values, IDs, names and number formats exactly as
  formatted.

# Fields of Float and near-critical

Generated from reference/spec.json by the catalog build. Each slot of reference/report.md is copied from one field of one call; write it in its format, never compute it.

## Calls

1. fa = p6_float_analysis(project="{project}"): float statistics and distribution of the open activities, data date.
2. fp = p6_float_paths(project="{project}", limit=30): float paths of the last F9: summary per path and the activities in path order.
3. nc = p6_critical_path(project="{project}", float_threshold_days={near_days}, min_float_days=0, limit=30): near-critical activities: total float above 0 and at or below near_days; project counts.

## Formats

- text: the value as returned
- int: the whole number, a comma between thousands: 1,227
- date: the first 10 characters: YYYY-MM-DD
- datetime: the first 16 characters: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM
- n0: the number as written in the result rounded to a whole number, halves away from zero, a comma between thousands: 12,345
- n1: the same to 1 decimal: 12,345.6 (-104274.95 gives -104,275.0)
- n2: the same to 2 decimals: 12,345.67
- pct1: the same to 1 decimal, then %: 49.7%
- flag: yes for true, no for false
- id_name: the two fields joined: ID - Name (the ID alone when the name is null, the none text when the ID is null)
- list: the items of the list in their order, joined by a comma and a space: in_progress, finishing
- A null value is written as the slot's or column's none text (n/a unless stated).
- [if: slot] is true for true, a number other than 0, a text or list that is not empty.

## Arguments

- {project}: Project ID as shown in P6, as given
- {near_days}: Near-critical threshold: total float above 0 and at or below this many days (each activity's calendar); 10 when the user gives none, as given

## Units

- d: days of each activity's calendar (hours / hours per day)
- %: percent
- count: a count

## Slots

| Slot | Field (call.path) | Unit | Format | None | Meaning |
|-|-|-|-|-|-|
| data_date | fa.schedule_state.data_date |  | date | n/a | data date of the project |
| last_f9 | fa.schedule_state.last_schedule_date |  | datetime | n/a | last schedule run (F9) in P6 |
| stale | fa.schedule_state.stale |  | flag | n/a | this server changed the project after the last F9 |
| activities | fa.scope.activities | count | int | n/a | open activities analysed: not completed, LOE and WBS summary left out |
| no_tf | fa.no_value.total_float | count | int | n/a | open activities without a total float |
| tf_min | fa.stats.tf_min_d | d | n1 | n/a | lowest total float |
| tf_max | fa.stats.tf_max_d | d | n1 | n/a | highest total float |
| tf_mean | fa.stats.tf_mean_d | d | n1 | n/a | mean total float |
| tf_median | fa.stats.tf_median_d | d | n1 | n/a | median total float |
| negative | fa.stats.negative_tf | count | int | n/a | open activities with negative total float |
| zero | fa.stats.zero_tf | count | int | n/a | open activities with total float exactly 0 |
| critical | fa.stats.critical | count | int | n/a | critical open activities under the project's definition |
| critical_definition | fa.stats.critical_definition |  | text | n/a | the project's definition of critical |
| tf_not_whole | fa.stats.tf_not_whole_days | count | int | n/a | total floats that are not a whole number of days |
| ranges_covered | fa.all_ranges_covered |  | flag | n/a | range counts plus activities without float equal the activities analysed |
| fp_source | fp.source |  | text | n/a | float_path (P6 multiple float paths) or driving_path_flag (no float path stored) |
| longest_path | nc.counts.longest_path | count | int | n/a | open activities on the longest path (driving path flag) |
| within_near | nc.counts.total_float | count | int | n/a | open activities with total float at or below near_days, critical included |
| near_total | nc.total | count | int | n/a | near-critical activities: total float above 0 and at or below near_days |
| near_definition | nc.definition |  | text | n/a | the threshold used by the near-critical table |

## Table buckets

Float ranges in days: below the first edge, [a, b) below zero, exactly 0, (a, b] above zero, above the last edge.

Rows: fa.buckets, in the order returned, at most 12 (a dict gives one row per item: its key is _key, a plain value _value).
When the list holds more than 12 items, add the line: Only the first 12 ranges are shown.
No rows: write 'No open activity.' instead of the table (nothing when the call failed).

| Column | Field (row path) | Unit | Format | None | In totals row |
|-|-|-|-|-|-|
| Range (d) | label | d | text | n/a |  |
| Total float | total_float | count | int | n/a |  |
| Total float % | tf_pct | % | pct1 | n/a |  |
| Free float | free_float | count | int | n/a |  |
| Free float % | ff_pct | % | pct1 | n/a |  |

## Table paths

One row per float path (1 = the most critical), over every page.

Rows: fp.paths, in the order returned, at most 10 (a dict gives one row per item: its key is _key, a plain value _value).
When the list holds more than 10 items, add the line: Only the first 10 float paths are shown.
No rows: write 'P6 stored no float paths for this project: the next table lists the longest path activities (driving path flag) by start.' instead of the table (nothing when the call failed).

| Column | Field (row path) | Unit | Format | None | In totals row |
|-|-|-|-|-|-|
| Path | path |  | int | n/a |  |
| Activities | activities | count | int | n/a |  |
| Min total float (d) | min_tf_d | d | n1 | n/a |  |
| Max total float (d) | max_tf_d | d | n1 | n/a |  |
| Finish | finish |  | date | n/a |  |

## Table path_rows

Open activities of the float paths in P6 order: path, then order on the path.

Rows: fp.rows, in the order returned, at most 30.
When fp.next_offset is not null, add the line: Showing the first <returned> of <total> float path activities. (returned and total of fp).
No rows: write 'No open activity on a float path.' instead of the table (nothing when the call failed).

| Column | Field (row path) | Unit | Format | None | In totals row |
|-|-|-|-|-|-|
| Path | float_path |  | int | none |  |
| Order | float_path_order |  | int | none |  |
| Activity | task_code + task_name |  | id_name | n/a |  |
| Total float (d) | total_float_d | d | n1 | n/a |  |
| Early start | early_start_date |  | date | n/a |  |
| Early finish | early_end_date |  | date | n/a |  |

## Table near

Near-critical activities: total float above 0 and at or below near_days, by total float then start.

Rows: nc.rows, in the order returned, at most 30.
When nc.next_offset is not null, add the line: Showing the first <returned> of <total> activities. (returned and total of nc).
No rows: write 'No open activity with total float above 0 and at or below this threshold.' instead of the table (nothing when the call failed).

| Column | Field (row path) | Unit | Format | None | In totals row |
|-|-|-|-|-|-|
| Activity | task_code + task_name |  | id_name | n/a |  |
| Status | status_code |  | text | n/a |  |
| Total float (d) | total_float_d | d | n1 | n/a |  |
| Free float (d) | free_float_d | d | n1 | n/a |  |
| Remaining duration (d) | rem_dur_d | d | n1 | n/a |  |
| Early finish | early_end_date |  | date | n/a |  |
| Float path | float_path |  | int | none |  |

## Cross-checks (equal values)

- same data date in the three calls: fa.schedule_state.data_date = fp.schedule_state.data_date = nc.schedule_state.data_date
- same number of open activities: fa.scope.activities = nc.counts.open
- same negative float count: fa.stats.negative_tf = nc.counts.negative_float
